text:
Edmonton hosts Anaheim tonight with both teams one night removed from a rest day and each carrying its own strain. The Ducks won 5-4 at Vancouver two nights ago behind a Cutter Gauthier hat trick, and they're 3-1-1 in their last five, but they're without A.J. Greer and Ryan Poehling. The Oilers saw a three-game winning streak end in a shootout loss at New Jersey, and they're missing Zach Hyman (neck) and Isaac Howard. It's also a rematch of last spring's first-round series, which the Ducks won in six.

The numbers favor Edmonton, with our model projecting 3.33 expected goals to Anaheim's 2.84. Expected goals measure the quality of chances. The Ducks have taken only 44% of them at five on five and allow 3.48 per 60 minutes, while the Oilers allow 2.67. Edmonton's power play (0.88 expected goals a game) meets a Ducks penalty kill allowing 0.82, and Anaheim takes 5.1 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Laurent Brossoit (-1.3 goals saved above expected, meaning he has allowed more than average goalies would on the same shots) and Matt Tomkins (+1.4) are both working from tiny samples.

Gauthier has goals in three straight and is 40% to score tonight; Leo Carlsson is 72% for a point. Connor McDavid carries a 16-game point streak and is 93% for a point, with Leon Draisaitl at 46% to score. Among our under-the-radar picks, Kasperi Kapanen, now up to 19:46 a night with Hyman out, is 46% for a point, and fourth-liner Filip Hallander is 12% to score, both against a Ducks defense that gives up the fifth-most expected goals per 60. They're players to watch, not locks.
